subject: Reserved commit term & start-gate options — Suncrest Health
messages:
From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@suncrest.health>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Exploring reserved commit options and throughput guarantees

Hi Irene + Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week — Suncrest is seriously evaluating Redwood Dedicated for our LLM inference layer (clinical summarization + anonymized search). Procurement asked me to put requirements in writing so you can scope reserved commit options. High-level: we expect ~120M tokens/month initially, peaking to ~400M tokens/month in 9 months.

Key asks:
- Pricing across 12 / 24 / 36 month reserved commits (please show committed GPU-pool equivalents or vGPU sizing).
- Throughput guarantees (p99 latency targets for 512-token responses, and sustained tokens/sec per pool).
- Ramp schedule flexibility — we have a planned pilot (soft start) Jan 15 2027, then phased production rollouts.
- Any credits/discounts for financial commit and an option to pause or slow ramp for regulatory review.

I'm attaching a short requirements PDF (procurement asked for attachments). Procurement timeline: they need commercial terms by Oct 20 to hit internal Q4 review.

Cc'ing our procurement lead (procure@suncrest.health) and Priya Shah, who owns platform integration.

Thanks,
Tom
--
Tom Alvarez
Head of Platform Engineering
Suncrest Health
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@suncrest.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-04T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring reserved commit options and throughput guarantees

Hi Tom — great to get this written down, appreciate the timeline. Attaching a throughput model and an initial SOW draft to make the numbers concrete (Suncrest_Throughput_Model_v2.xlsx, SOW-dedicated-commit-draft.pdf).

A few clarifying questions that will shape the commit sizing and discounts:
- Can you confirm the expected token distribution by model family (e.g., 50% long-form summarization at ~512 tokens/request, 50% short prompts at ~64 tokens)?
- Are there predictable daily peaks (e.g., business hours only) or evenly distributed traffic?
- Do you need hard p99 latency SLOs, or would a best-effort latency with credits for missed throughput be acceptable for phase 1?

High-level options (rough, will formalize after you confirm the above):
- 12-month: modest discount, minimal start-gate (30-day activation window), GPU pool sized to expected peak, 3-month ramp tolerance.
- 24-month: material discount, ability to define a 90-day soft start (reduced billing in first 90 days), staged tranches for scaling the GPU pool.
- 36-month: deepest discount, commitment to fixed pricing across term, larger upfront capacity reservation and priority routing.

Ben — can you put together a quick table with preliminary GPU-equivalent sizing (A100-class equivalents) for the 120M -> 400M tokens/month band and add rough $/token guidance per term?

Tom — if those timelines work, we can get a formal commercial proposal to you by Oct 14 so procurement has time for review.

Best,
Irene

Irene Choi
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@suncrest.health>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, procure@suncrest.health
Date: 2026-10-06T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring reserved commit options and throughput guarantees

Irene — thanks, the timeline looks doable. Answers below so you can firm numbers up:

- Token mix: roughly 60% summarization (~512 tokens avg), 35% short prompts (~64 tokens), 5% embeddings/rerank (bursty).
- Peaks: weekday business hours (US central) with ~2.5x spike between 9am-3pm local.
- Latency: For production we need p95 < 300ms for 64-token responses and p99 < 1200ms for 512-token responses. For pilot a best-effort with financial credits if throughput isn't met would be OK.

Preferred commercial stance: 24-month preferred if we can get a 15-20% effective discount off list and a 90-day soft start where billing is at 50% for committed capacity while we finalize integration. We'd also like a clause to temporarily slow ramp (not cancel) for up to 60 days for regulatory reviews, with reasonable notice.

Attached: procurement_timeline.xlsx (procurement will push on pricing tiers).

Tom
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@suncrest.health>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-09T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Exploring reserved commit options and throughput guarantees

Tom — appreciate the detail. Based on your mix and peak profile I ran three sizing scenarios (see summary below; full workbook attached in the SOW package). All pricing below is illustrative until legal signs off on SOW.

Sizing & pricing (A100-class equivalence):
- Pilot stage (soft start): 6 A100-equivalent GPUs -> supports ~120M tokens/month baseline with headroom for spikes.
- Phase production: 18 A100-equivalent GPUs -> supports up to ~400M tokens/month with target p99 latency margins.

Commercial counterproposal:
- 12-month: 10% discount off list; billing begins at full rate at activation; 30-day activation window.
- 24-month: 18% discount; 90-day soft start at 50% billing for committed pool; 12-month minimum billing floor (i.e., while the contract is 24m, billing protection for Redwood to cover allocation).
- 36-month: 22% discount; 90-day soft start at 30% billing for committed pool; accelerated capacity priority.

Ramp & start-gate approach we recommend:
- Soft start window (90 days): Pilot capacity at 33%-50% of committed GPUs depending on term.
- Tranche 1 (Day 91-180): increase to 60% committed capacity.
- Tranche 2 (Day 181-365): full committed capacity.

Throughput guarantees & credits:
- Guarantee: p95/p99 latency bands as you requested for listed workloads when running on committed capacity + standard shared-buffer margins.
- Credit: If p99 latency exceeds target for >3 days in a rolling 30-day window, customer receives service credits equal to X% of monthly committed bill (we propose a sliding scale; legal will draft exact percentages).

Pause-for-compliance: We can include a pause-for-compliance clause (up to 60 days) where billing is reduced to 25% of committed rate while the pool is preserved. That preserves your seat while acknowledging our capacity economics.

Next steps: I'll convert this into a formal commercial term sheet and attach a redlineable SOW. If agreeable we can target Oct 14 for a first-draft proposal for procurement. HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/DEAL-2397

-ben

Ben Carter
Head of Dedicated Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@suncrest.health>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, procure@suncrest.health, Priya Shah <pshah@suncrest.health>
Date: 2026-10-12T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring reserved commit options and throughput guarantees

Ben/Irene — this looks reasonable and addresses the main concerns. Two quick asks before we engage legal:
1) Please quantify the monthly committed bill in $ for the 24-month scenario (given the 18% discount) with the 18 A100-equivalent pool so procurement can model cash flow.
2) Add explicit language that during the 90-day soft start we will have a dedicated onboarding runbook and prioritized support (SLA for escalation).

If you can send the redlined SOW + a numbers table by Oct 14 we'll put it on the procurement review. If procurement signs off, target pilot activation Jan 15 2027 with tranche increases as outlined.

Thanks — Tom
--
Tom Alvarez
Head of Platform Engineering
Suncrest Health
